claim: The original paper's protocol contains three evaluation leaks: augmentation before the split, a recording-level random split, and checkpoint selection on the test split
criterion: Protocol stated in the paper text and code
notes: Paper §II.E and §III; code at 3ec7dc6. Verified by reading both on 2026-10-23

claim: Under the original protocol the model reaches about the reported 95.67% accuracy
notes: X1:secondary_metrics L0.accuracy.mean is 0.878 (20 seeds), 7.9 pts below the paper; released-code class sizes differ from the paper for two classes (see X1 limitations). Fidelity grid (X1-F): the published code cannot run as released; under batch 32/full × sigmoid/Keras-2 hard sigmoid the mean is 0.79–0.88, and 0 of 80 runs reach the paper's lowest reported run (0.949). Best 10 of 20 adds ~2 points. Not reproducible from the published materials

claim: Removing the leaks lowers performance by at least 15 points
criterion: L0 − L3 ≥ 0.15 (balanced accuracy, the protocol's primary metric)
notes: Balanced accuracy 0.872 → 0.385 (chance 0.167). Raw accuracy 0.878 → 0.598, but accuracy is not comparable across rungs (test COPD share 22.5% vs 59%) and at L3 equals the always-COPD baseline (0.591). Criterion was first evaluated on accuracy; corrected per D-19

claim: 631 clips of the Kaggle Asthma Detection Dataset V2 are verbatim cuts of ICBHI recordings
criterion: count == 631 with a clean score gap
notes: min overlap NCC vs max non-overlap NCC are in the summary JSON

claim: 316 Kaggle V2 clips are cuts of KAUH recordings, and its filename patient groups mix real patients
criterion: count == 316; 57 of 64 groups mixed
notes: Reproduced by research/tools/kaggle_group_check.py (57/64 KAUH, 35/98 ICBHI)

claim: Disease labels are confounded with recording source and device in the merged cohort
criterion: e.g. all COPD from ICBHI; KAUH-derived training audio non-healthy/non-COPD before round 2b
notes: Before round 2b all COPD was ICBHI; in split v3 793 of 805 COPD recordings (64 of 68 patients) are ICBHI, 12 recordings / 4 patients KAUH. KAUH-derived training audio was non-healthy/non-COPD before round 2b. Tables generated by research/tools/dataset_tables.py [Independent audit 2026-10-23: corrected 'all COPD from ICBHI']

claim: Every representation decodes the dataset of origin and the ICBHI device more easily than the disease
criterion: probe(dataset) > probe(disease) and probe(device) > probe(disease) for all representations
notes: Linear probes only; patient-grouped 3-fold. [Independent audit 2026-10-23: the probes have different chance levels (dataset 2–3 classes, device 4, disease 5); the claim still holds after normalising each by its chance level]

claim: A model trained on the confounded data fails on an external site: KAUH healthy and COPD patients are predicted asthma
criterion: patient accuracy == 0 on 45 in-label patients
notes: Exact 95% CI 0–7.9% (research/tools/exact_ci.py). Bandwidth explanation tested in X2 (C-09)

claim: The external failure is a site/device shortcut rather than a 4 kHz bandwidth artifact
criterion: ICBHI audio in KAUH's 4 kHz format is not pushed toward asthma
notes: Asthma share at 4 kHz: COPD 0.040, healthy 0.083 (1 of 12), bronchial 0.045, vs ~1.0 for KAUH patients; accuracy does drop (COPD 0.905→0.850, healthy 0.833→0.500); small healthy n. Exact 95% CIs: COPD 14/346 → 2.2–6.7%; healthy 1/12 → 0.2–38.5% (uninformative); safe wording: not explained by sample rate alone [Independent audit 2026-10-23: the exact CIs treat 346 recordings from 26 patients as independent, so they are too narrow; quote them as recording-level]

claim: Adding some patients of an external site to training improves accuracy on other patients of that site (within-site adaptation; not cross-site generalization)
criterion: holdout in-label accuracy ≥ 0.30 above EXP-013
notes: 17/24 (70.8%, exact CI 48.9–87.4%) vs 0/24: met on accuracy, but only through healthy (17/18); COPD 0/5 (CI 0–52%), balanced accuracy 31.5% ≈ 3-class chance. Out-of-label KAUH predictions moved from asthma to healthy: site-dominant label, not disease. Safe wording: 'exposure to a site's healthy patients made the model call that site's patients healthy' Sensitivity (C-21): removing 3 holdout recordings that are byte-identical to training-side asthma audio gives 18/24 (healthy 18/18); COPD unchanged at 0/5.

claim: Pretrained embeddings are more site-robust than MFCC RespiNet
evidence_refs: EXP-R2A-*, EXP-R2B-* shortcut metrics; X3 per member
criterion: non-overlapping CIs
notes: Mixed results so far: OPERA-CE worse on off-device COPD, HeAR better; no CI separation shown

claim: The abstention rule flags out-of-label audio
criterion: out-of-label rate above in-label rate with a patient-bootstrap CI excluding 0
status: unsupported for models without KAUH healthy/COPD patients in training; weakly supported after
notes: Pre-2b models (no KAUH healthy/COPD patients in training): Δ +0.3 to +9.4 points, every CI includes 0, and about two thirds of their (all wrong) in-label external calls were not abstained. Round 2b (KAUH patients in training): 64.2% vs 45.8%, Δ +18.4 [2.8, 33.6]; in-label accuracy 69.4% → 79.5% on accepted recordings. Not an OOD detector: a site shortcut makes the model confidently wrong

claim: Leak-free in-cohort test accuracy of the served round-2b model
criterion: reported with 95% CI
notes: Patient accuracy 75.51% (95% CI 63.3–87.8%), 49 patients; balanced 74.87%. In-cohort only; never presented as clinical performance. [Independent audit 2026-10-23: previously cited EXP-012, the archived round-2 model, whose metrics also describe epoch-64 weights rather than its served epoch-67 file]. Without the 6 Kaggle-remainder test patients: 74.4% accuracy, 68.0% balanced (TESTPRED)

claim: RespiNet with cuDNN GRUs trains about twice as fast with similar accuracy
evidence_refs: EXP-R2A-D3 vs EXP-R2A-D0 (run_D3.json, run_D0.json fold minutes)
notes: Engineering result; not a paper claim. [Independent audit 2026-10-23: D3 also switches SpecAugment from per-batch to per-sample, so the speed-up is not attributable to cuDNN alone]

claim: Within a single diagnosis, the recording source is still predictable from every representation (e.g. healthy: ICBHI vs Kaggle vs KAUH), so the features carry acquisition differences independent of disease
criterion: probe(source | diagnosis) well above chance for well-powered diagnoses
notes: Healthy (19/11/15 patients): 0.82 MFCC stats, 0.91–0.96 embeddings vs chance 0.33. COPD ICBHI vs KAUH rests on only 3 KAUH patients (MFCC stats at chance 0.50). Linear probes, patient-grouped 3-fold

claim: The cross-correlation copy detector finds copies reliably: 99 of 100 synthetic degraded cuts matched to their true ICBHI source; no KAUH recording matches ICBHI
criterion: recall ≥ 0.95 on synthetic cuts; 0 false matches on an unrelated dataset
notes: One miss (score 0.621, correct source but below the 0.75 threshold) → counts of 631/316 are lower bounds. Blind listening check (one rater, the user; 2026-10-23) of the 20 hardest real cases (10 lowest-scoring matches, 10 highest-scoring non-matches): 19 decided, all agree with the detector (exact 95% CI 82.4–100%), 1 unsure (a non-match); includes the weakest match (NCC 0.795). A second independent rater would allow inter-rater agreement. Independent landmark-fingerprint detector agrees on all 631 ICBHI and 313 of 316 KAUH matches with none extra (C-31). A package for a second human rater is prepared (listening_rater2.zip, blank sheet); not yet rated, so inter-rater agreement is still pending

claim: In the 2021 protocol the largest leak is augmented copies crossing the split; patient overlap and checkpoint selection on the test set each add a further 7–13 points (their order is not statistically separable)
evidence_refs: X1:secondary_metrics (L0, L1, L2, L2T, L3, L3T; balanced_drop_*); backend/artifacts/experiments/leakage_ladder/summary.json
criterion: factorial split unit × selection with 20 seeds per cell
notes: Balanced accuracy (validation-selected): sample 0.799 → recording 0.511 (−0.287) → patient 0.384 (−0.127). Test-selection inflation: +0.073 / +0.075 / +0.107 (sample / recording / patient). Sample-level splits also put augmented copies in the test set, so that step mixes two effects [Independent audit 2026-10-23: recording→patient drop 0.127 ± 0.142 (sd over seeds) vs selection 0.07–0.11: ordering not separable; claim reworded]

claim: Within one Kaggle-V2-trained model, ICBHI recordings that were copied into Kaggle are classified far more accurately than clean ICBHI recordings of the same class
criterion: difference > 0 with a patient-bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0
notes: COPD 81.1% (26 patients) vs 41.5% (38): +39.5 points [26.9, 50.9]. Bronchial 62.5% (7) vs 13.2% (22): +49.3 [23.4, 82.1]. Different patients in the two groups; uploader selection cannot be excluded; replicated with a second seed. Seed 43: COPD +51.4 [38.9, 63.6], bronchial +65.5 [32.0, 85.4]

claim: Removing the ICBHI copies from Kaggle-V2 training removes most of the model's accuracy on those copied ICBHI recordings
criterion: paired difference > 0 with CI excluding 0
status: verified for healthy and pneumonia; not for bronchial
notes: Healthy 96.2% → 15.4% (21 patients, +80.8 [65.4, 93.6]); pneumonia 85.3% → 32.4% (6 patients, CI 27.3–71.4); bronchial 62.5% → 43.8% (n.s., CI −25.0 to 61.5). Confounded by the class set (no COPD without copies) and training size [Independent audit 2026-10-23: the criterion holds only for healthy and pneumonia]. Seed 43 replicates: healthy 92.3% → 34.6% (CI of Δ 36–77), pneumonia 94.1% → 38.2% (30–75), bronchial n.s. again

claim: Kaggle V2 contains more ICBHI/KAUH material than its description discloses
criterion: count comparable in units with the disclosure
notes: The description says 'ICBHI dataset: 212 samples' and 'about 170 samples'. We find 631 clips from 187 distinct ICBHI recordings and 316 clips from 115 KAUH recordings: more clips but fewer source recordings than disclosed, so the comparison depends on what 'samples' means. Safe wording: the description discloses the sources but not that recordings were cut into several clips presented as separate samples with non-patient identifiers, nor that all of Kaggle's COPD class is ICBHI audio

claim: The public KAUH dataset contains byte-identical recordings filed under different patients with conflicting diagnoses (healthy vs asthma)
criterion: SHA-256 equality
notes: 4 identical groups in 336 files; 3 pair a healthy patient with an asthma patient (patients 100↔101 in two filters, 76↔77), 1 is one patient under two filter names (9). Two holdout healthy patients (900100, 900076) share audio with asthma patients in the served model's validation/training data: X3 sensitivity without those 3 recordings gives 18/24 (healthy 18/18, COPD still 0/5) vs 17/24 as registered. Found by the independent audit. Fix: data/kauh_external_holdout_manifest_v2.csv drops patients 76 and 100 (X3 on v2: 16/22, healthy 16/16, COPD 0/5); experiments/external.py refuses audio-linked holdout patients

claim: The adopted round-2b fusion outperforms the reference R′ (D0 + YAMNet) in cross-validation
criterion: Holm-adjusted one-sided p < 0.05 within the pre-registered family
notes: +4.8 balanced accuracy, raw p 0.048 → Holm 0.164 over the 4 pre-registered fusions (1.0 over all 35 reported). The adoption followed its fixed rule (P ≥ 0.90), so it stands; only superiority must not be claimed. Second audit: the 'pre-registered' family of 4 ignores that D3_x3 was itself picked among six D3 variants, so 0.164 is optimistic; a 20,000-draw rerun gives raw 0.043 and Holm about 0.17

claim: A rule that predicts the disease from recording source and stethoscope alone, with no audio, rivals the trained models
criterion: no-audio rule within a few points of the model, or better
notes: Split v3: rule 84.1% vs model 82.0% recording accuracy; patient balanced 70.8% vs 74.9%. Split v2: 87.8% vs 81.2%; 68.5% vs 71.9%. X1 L3 (2020 network, leak-free): device rule 0.440 vs network 0.384 balanced accuracy, network better in 7/20 paired seeds. Paired patient bootstrap on split v3 (TESTPRED): model − rule +4.1 points [−6.9, +16.1], P(model better) 0.77; no CI for the other comparisons. The rule's definition was chosen among two after seeing the test split: source alone reaches only 0.522 patient balanced accuracy (v3), source + stethoscope 0.708; and the Kaggle part of the key (clips cut from KAUH vs unknown) comes from audio matching

claim: Normal vs abnormal: in-cohort AUROC 0.94, but at chance on the external KAUH site for models with no KAUH healthy or COPD patients in training
criterion: external CI includes 0.5 while in-cohort CI excludes it
notes: In cohort 0.94 [0.87, 0.99] (49 test patients). External: pre-round-2 0.48 [0.35, 0.62], round-2 0.47 [0.34, 0.60] (72 patients); these models did see 316 Kaggle clips cut from 40 KAUH patients (asthma, bronchial, pneumonia only). After round 2b 0.83 [0.71, 0.94] on the holdout (within site). Comparable design to Ong Ly et al. 2024 (0.97 → 0.60)

claim: Normal-vs-abnormal discrimination does not reliably transfer to a recording source left out of training
criterion: held-out AUROC near 0.5 while within-cohort is high
notes: Held-out AUROC lies in 0.38–0.59 in 9 of 12 representation × source cells (10 of 15 with AST); exceptions: Kaggle remainder (YAMNet 0.87, OPERA-CE 0.69, HeAR 0.66, AST 0.80) and AST on the KAUH site (0.21, below range). 11 of 12 held-out CIs include 0.5 (12 of 15 with AST). Within cohort 0.51–0.96, with two weak cells (OPERA-CE/ICBHI 0.51, MFCC/Kaggle remainder 0.61). Caveats (second audit): the KAUH-site group is confounded with file origin (its 15 normal patients are raw KAUH files, 29 of its 32 abnormal patients are Kaggle clips cut from KAUH); the ICBHI group's normals are Meditron-recorded children; the Kaggle remainder's 'patients' are filename groups, so within-cohort AUROCs may be inflated. These cells measure confounding by construction. Frozen embeddings + linear heads, development patients only. Leave-one-device-out is impossible (healthy ICBHI = Meditron only)

claim: The recording source is decodable from audio without breath sounds (an acquisition signature)
criterion: source probes from non-breath segments well above chance
notes: Quietest 10% of frames: dataset 0.79, device 0.81, source within diagnosis 0.93–0.98 (asthma, bronchial, healthy, pneumonia); first/last 100 ms: 0.76 / 0.83 / 0.93–0.96. COPD (source within COPD, only 3 KAUH patients) is lower: 0.77 / 0.72. Safe wording: 'an acquisition signature exists that a model can exploit' (not that it does). Quietest frames may contain faint breath

claim: Age is confounded with source and label: ICBHI's healthy class is entirely children, KAUH's healthy patients are adults
criterion: age distributions by source and class
notes: ICBHI healthy: 26 patients aged 0–16 (median 5); ICBHI COPD median 69; KAUH healthy median 32 (cohort) / 42 (holdout). The external failure therefore has an age explanation alongside site/device; wording: site/acquisition/population confounding

claim: Adding KAUH patients to training raises recognition of the site's healthy patients as more are added, but not of its COPD patients
criterion: monotone dose-response with k
notes: Healthy recall 0 / 0.16 / 0.67 / 0.94 at k = 0 / 4 / 9 / 18; COPD recall 0 at every k (only 3 KAUH COPD development patients); AUROC 0.66 → 0.88. Embedding members only; within-site; diagnostic reuse of the v2 holdout

claim: A stronger general-audio model (frozen AST) is better in cohort but has the highest dataset-of-origin probe and fails on an unseen-source cell
criterion: in-cohort gain with no cross-site gain
notes: CV patient balanced accuracy 78.3% (HeAR 71.6%; +6.7 [1.5, 12.6]); dataset-of-origin probe 0.94 (highest, no CI); on the ICBHI-device probe AST is third (0.87) and on source within COPD the lowest, so 'strongest source signature' is not supported beyond the dataset probe. KAUH-site held-out AUROC 0.21 vs within-cohort 0.95, but that LOSO cell is confounded with file origin (raw KAUH files vs Kaggle clips cut from KAUH; see C-25). Frozen, not fine-tuned; not pre-registered, so no serving change. Fine-tuning (AST-FT, C-30) did not change this

claim: Fine-tuning the best frozen general-audio model does not help: it is not better than frozen embeddings or the adopted fusion in cross-validation, and has lower off-device COPD sensitivity than frozen AST
criterion: paired CV comparison with frozen AST and the adopted fusion
notes: Patient balanced accuracy 74.4% vs frozen AST 78.3% (paired −9.2 to +1.1 points, P(improve) 0.075) and vs adopted fusion 74.9% (−6.3 to +5.3, P 0.42). Off-device COPD sensitivity 62.1% (116 recordings, 30 patients) vs 85.3% frozen: −23.3 points, patient-cluster CI [−36.8, −10.4]; vs the adopted fusion's 75.0%: −12.9 [−28.9, +3.9], not distinguishable. Meditron 56.2% / 56.2% / 61.5%. Best epochs 5/2/2; 12.6 GPU-minutes. One seed, noisy inner validation, no tuning (D-28); weights not kept

claim: A second, independent algorithm (landmark fingerprinting) finds the same copies as the cross-correlation audit, and none the audit missed
criterion: agreement with the 631/316 matches; zero additional detections
notes: ICBHI 631/631 found, same source recording in all; KAUH 313/316 (the 3 missed are clips ≤ 0.7 s); 0 additional on either set; the 10 differences in best KAUH reference are all ties between byte-identical KAUH files (patients 100/101, 76/77, 9). Fixed settings (D-30): chance votes median 8, p99 16, max 21 on 300 time-reversed windows vs threshold 25 (thin margin; real matches median 239). Synthetic recall 93/100 (first detector 99/100). Same 100–1,000 Hz band as the first detector. The clips cut from the audio filed as 'healthy' KAUH patients 100 and 76 carry Kaggle's asthma/wheezing label, suggesting those two 'normal' files are mislabeled copies of asthma recordings (inference, not verified)
